Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Semantic Web [IT_4412]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                A software company wants to maintain a digital contact list of its employees to share information       (5)  
  easily across different departments and applications. Each contact should include the employee's  
  A)           name, phone number, and email address in a structured format that can be exchanged between  
  systems. Apply your understanding of XML structure to develop an XML document that represents  
  the company's contact list, ensuring that each contact entry contains the required details - name,  
  phone number, and email - in a well-formed and organized manner.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           RDF data can be represented using different syntaxes such as RDF/XML, Turtle, and JSON-LD,              (5)  
  but all convey the same underlying data model. Apply your understanding of RDF representations  
  to explain how these different syntaxes maintain the same semantic meaning. Develop a brief  
  theoretical explanation highlighting how RDF's triple-based structure ensures data consistency  
  across multiple formats.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                An e-commerce company manages a large product catalog that includes information about                   (5)  
  products, suppliers, prices, and categories. All this information is represented and stored using RDF  
  A)           to enable semantic querying and data integration across multiple vendors. The company wants to  
  analyse supplier performance and pricing trends using SPARQL queries. Analyse how SPARQL  
  queries, using various filters, pattern matching, and construct clauses, can be designed to extract all  
  suppliers offering products priced below ₹1000.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           A healthcare startup is planning to design and implement an ontology for managing and integrating (5)  
  patient health records. Examine how adopting different ontology development approaches could  
  influence the accuracy, consistency, and interoperability of the resulting healthcare data model.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                A job portal system aims to build an intelligent platform that can match candidates with suitable job   (5)  
  roles based on their skills. To enable smarter data representation and reasoning, the development  
  A)           team decides to use OWL2 to design an ontology that is compatible with RDF/RDFS standards.  
  Apply OWL2 to create an ontology ensuring RDF/RDFS compatibility.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           A semantic reasoning module in a chatbot must infer facts quickly. Choose an OWL2 profile that          (5)  
  
  Page #1

suits this need and explain how description logic supports reasoning under constraints.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                        In an online certification system, once a badge is awarded, it cannot be revoked. Develop a             (5)  
  monotonic SWRL rule to model this and explain its significance in maintaining trust.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                In an energy grid, power supply rules change dynamically depending on demand. Develop RuleML- (5)  
  based non-monotonic rules to capture this scenario.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)                        A travel agency wants to create a system that combines flight details, hotel options, and local         (5)  
  attractions to help customers plan their trips easily. To build this system efficiently, the agency  
  A)                decides to use existing travel ontologies instead of starting from scratch. Apply your understanding  
  of ontology reuse and extension to develop a domain ontology model that integrates flight, hotel,  
  and attraction data, ensuring that the information is interoperable and reusable across different  
  travel services.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                Two universities maintain their own academic ontologies - one uses "Course" and "Instructor," while (5)  
  the other uses "Module" and "Teacher" to represent similar concepts. To enable data sharing and  
  integration between their systems, they need to perform ontology mapping.  
  Apply your understanding of ontology mapping to develop a method that aligns equivalent classes  
  and properties (e.g., Course ↔ Module, Instructor ↔ Teacher) so that data from both universities  
  can be integrated and queried seamlessly across systems.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
